BETWEEN THE FOOD CHAIN, THE LINGUISTIC CODE AND THE FORESTRY CODE
With the presuppositions of ephemerity and invisibility, that joint action of ingesting the Portuguese language
undertaken by the tamarins (as animals that eat bananas and suffixes, from the point of view of linguistic morphology) provoked by the semantic trap built by Barja, what is given us to see is the record in
real time and with a posteriori documentation, captured by security cameras, of the composition of the words and
their later disappearance with the intervention of their suffixes/simians.
I return, then, to the threads/lines/trails of Araucária Street. I think of writing and of inscriptions, so often imagined
by the city dweller when confronted with a sky covered with electrical networks. I think of the separation and juxtaposition between nature and culture that the work provokes. The first two poetic equations (the oldest ones) carry
in themselves the sign of discourse, the direct relation with the letters articulated into meanings. We could even speak of
a pendulation between the thesis (developed within the academy ) and the antithesis ( generated from the former and creating the
polemic). Without a doubt, adjectives that name characteristics within the field of verbal language.  But the third
may be a detour: endemic is associated with contamination. With biological and biogeographical questions. In the game
about.1:
of opposing pairs, we guess the future appearance of the epide mic. With the new trap, there seems to be a
greater approximation to the act performed by the work. Moving from the chain of meaning to the food chain, it evokes
more directly what is seen in the video document: the materiality of writing feeding itself (at its own
expense). Yes, we have bananas.... Do we still have them?
The concreteness of the letters subjects them to the inaugural act of modernity in Brazilian art, the one that, starting from the week
of modern art of 22, configured itself as a Manifesto. Subverted by the artist’s poetic proposal – from the organization of the
picture-trap to the documentation of the attraction that bananas exert over the tamarins – it is travestied as Oswaldian anthropophagy. The work disappears in order to be able to take place. Paradox that comes to have unfoldings in the new presentation of the small semantic equations. The words, before their deglutition, are frozen and reproduced
in prints (freezing of the act, memento mori). In their initial configuration (of 1986), the first two works
were presented as a live performance, that is, the tamarins were taken inside the gallery. To eat
the idea they incarnated was something one could see live and in color (if the fruits/letters appealed to the animals).
Now, Barja offers us the performance of (self) destruction captured in the woods around the manor house. Poetry that is
made in the most basic concretization of the maintenance of life. From the conceptual point of view, there also seems to be a
displacement: if in their first configuration they were poetic possibilities; here, the emphasis shifts to the
documentation of the act (real and metaphorical). In that which induced us to a kind of resolution of the charade, now
it summons us to take a time (sometimes as long as that of field researchers) to be
eyewitnesses of the metaphorical transformation, the center of poetic production (verbal or imagistic).
Bon appétit!.
Marília Panitz  - Art criticism - Master in Theory and History of Art - UnB, Brasília. Professor at the Art Institute – UnB, Brasília.

As promise and threat, the mico (in flesh, bone and figurative sense) aligns itself with the bananas that form the two prefixes, already affirming its ephemerality (its destiny is as clear as the gaze the mico casts over them). The creature/box Cubo Cruz Lápide is eater and eaten at the same time, it swallows words like cubo and vomits them with the cruz. The inscriptions of its interior/reverse offer no meaning a priori, but the materiality of the words whispered as if affirming the fragility of the discourses we articulate. The other cross belongs to the group of works that composes the idea of the “Armadilhas Indígenas”, by Bené Fonteles: it is his Mognos Dei, one more obranome that plays at confusing references and inscribes its name with the wheat flour of the host, a raw material metaphorized in Christian practice, whose ritual presupposes the deglutition of the body of Christ. Which leads us to another reference certainly associated with the “anthropophagic practice” of so many letters... to that headboard without a bed of “DA²”, as equation and metonymic operation, a declaration of ideological affiliation. Prior to these experiments one could also point as a reference the “Poetamenos” of 1953, also by Augusto de Campos, defined as verbivocovisual, syncretic texts of word, sound and visual form that eliminate the phrase, the verse and potentiate a kind of colored alphabet soup whose meaning is organized in blocks, which demand from the spectator an important effort to combine them and find a meaning. Barja, interested in these intersemantic practices, also recovers the concept of Próbjeto, a term coined by the graphic artist and musician Rogério Duarte Guimarães close, in the sixties, to the work of Hélio Oiticica to define a project as object in itself; valuation of the artistic experience where the experiential and the processual acquire importance, even more than the realization of the idea itself, which opens possibilities of grouping between the text and the object (23).
